text:
For an overnight pellet-smoker cook at a campsite, I’d choose the **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2**. Its **2,073.6Wh capacity and 2,600W inverter** give you useful headroom for a cold night or charging other gear; the cited listing is **$899** ([buy the Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)). A 12-hour pellet-grill cook is estimated at roughly **450–750Wh**, depending on conditions and the grill’s draw. ([runtime and sizing details](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

For a lighter, lower-cost option, the **BLUETTI AC180 (1,152Wh)** is listed at **$449** and is sized for about one overnight cook—less spare capacity for other devices or especially cold, windy conditions. ([buy the AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180))

Before buying, check your smoker’s startup/igniter wattage: pellet grills have a brief higher draw when lighting, so the inverter’s surge rating matters. These recommendations are for **pellet grills**, not electric smokers with heating elements, which can draw far more power. ([pellet-grill sizing guidance](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill) · [electric-smoker power needs](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/))
